positions.stakeholder_concern: A variability-first definition would sweep in low-consequence informational features.
positions.requested_fda_action: Anchor risk to the consequence of acting on the output, not to whether the output is deterministic.
positions.public_summary: Supports a risk-based frame but argues variability alone is not a risk driver; risk should be tied to the clinical action the output can trigger.
positions.supporting_text: Variability in phrasing is not the hazard. The hazard is the clinical action a user is likely to take, and that should remain the organizing principle.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Risk assessed at clearance may not describe how the tool behaves at the bedside.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require manufacturers to state the behavioral envelope and what happens when a session drifts outside it.
positions.public_summary: Agrees risk should be action-linked, but notes that in practice the same tool moves between informational and directive use inside one conversation.
positions.supporting_text: In our pilot the same assistant summarized, then recommended, then produced an order draft, all in one exchange.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Point estimates hide tail behavior that matters clinically.
positions.requested_fda_action: Expect reporting of worst-case and tail performance, not only central tendency.
positions.public_summary: Supports distributional risk characterization: performance described as a distribution over responses rather than a point estimate.
positions.supporting_text: A mean accuracy figure tells a regulator very little about the responses that would actually cause harm.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Patients experience informational output as a recommendation.
positions.requested_fda_action: Treat patient-facing output as directive unless the sponsor shows otherwise.
positions.public_summary: Supports action-linked risk but asks that patient-facing outputs be treated as directive by default, since patients cannot always tell information from advice.
positions.supporting_text: A patient reading a confident paragraph does not see an informational feature. They see an instruction.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Sponsors need a shared vocabulary for autonomy levels.
positions.requested_fda_action: Adopt the independence axis with defined levels that sponsors can cite in labeling.
positions.public_summary: Supports the two-axis framing and says independence of action is the right first axis for generative functions.
positions.supporting_text: A shared scale for how independently a function acts would remove most of the ambiguity we see in early submissions.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Uncertainty about the bar delays programs more than the bar itself.
positions.requested_fda_action: Publish illustrative evidence packages for two or three representative device types.
positions.public_summary: Supports tiered evidence and asks FDA to publish worked examples so sponsors can predict the bar before starting studies.
positions.supporting_text: We can build to a demanding standard. We cannot build to an unstated one.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Retrospective benchmark performance has repeatedly failed to hold up in live workflow.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require at least one prospective evaluation in the intended setting for decision-supporting tools.
positions.public_summary: Supports tiering but argues any tool that reaches a clinical decision should require prospective evidence in a care setting.
positions.supporting_text: Benchmark performance and bedside performance have not matched in any deployment we have reviewed.

positions.stakeholder_concern: A uniform prospective study requirement is disproportionate at the low end.
positions.requested_fda_action: Keep prospective evidence tied to the highest tier only.
positions.public_summary: Opposes a fixed prospective requirement, arguing it would make lower-risk documentation tools economically unviable.
positions.supporting_text: A prospective study for a discharge summary drafting aid costs more than the product will ever return.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Inconsistent reporting makes submissions hard to compare.
positions.requested_fda_action: Define a minimum reporting set: population, prompts, failure modes, and human involvement.
positions.public_summary: Supports the tiered approach as drafted and asks FDA to specify reporting standards rather than study designs.
positions.supporting_text: Comparability is the missing ingredient. Standardize the reporting, not the design.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Investors cannot underwrite an evidence requirement that is not written down.
positions.requested_fda_action: State the evidence floor per tier so capital can be sized to it.
positions.public_summary: Supports proportional evidence and warns that an unstated bar is priced into every financing as regulatory risk.
positions.supporting_text: Every unstated requirement shows up in our models as a discount on the round.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Clinical confirmation for every function would slow iteration without adding safety.
positions.requested_fda_action: Let benchmarking substitute for clinical confirmation where consequence of error is limited.
positions.public_summary: Supports competency-based evaluation and asks that non-clinical benchmarking be allowed to carry more weight for lower-consequence functions.
positions.supporting_text: For a low-consequence function, a rigorous benchmark tells you more than a small clinical study does.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Security testing is currently reviewed separately from clinical risk.
positions.requested_fda_action: Fold adversarial evaluation into the device risk analysis rather than cybersecurity documentation alone.
positions.public_summary: Supports adversarial testing expectations and asks that retrieval poisoning and prompt injection be treated as clinical hazards, not IT controls.
positions.supporting_text: A retrieval poisoning event is not an IT incident. It is a clinical one.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Unstructured red-teaming produces unverifiable claims.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require a reported adversarial test matrix with residual failure rates.
positions.public_summary: Supports red-teaming requirements and proposes that sponsors report attack categories tested and the residual failure rate.
positions.supporting_text: Red-teaming without a reported matrix is an anecdote, not evidence.

positions.stakeholder_concern: The attack surface is assembled at the site, not by the sponsor.
positions.requested_fda_action: Define what sites must test locally when they connect their own content.
positions.public_summary: Supports adversarial testing but notes that site-specific retrieval content is where most injection risk lives, which premarket testing cannot see.
positions.supporting_text: The documents that poisoned our pilot were our own. No sponsor could have tested against them.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Model-only metrics say nothing about whether a clinician will catch an error.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require evaluation of the combined human-AI system, including override rates.
positions.public_summary: Supports explicit human-AI team evaluation and cites automation bias as the dominant failure mode observed in practice.
positions.supporting_text: The question is not whether the model is right. It is whether a tired clinician at hour ten will notice when it is not.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Manufacturers would be held to outcomes determined by local practice.
positions.requested_fda_action: Scope team evaluation to representative conditions and hold sites responsible for training fidelity.
positions.public_summary: Agrees in principle but says sponsors cannot control the human half, which varies by site, staffing, and training.
positions.supporting_text: We can characterize the tool under representative use. We cannot warrant a staffing model.

positions.stakeholder_concern: High override rates could be read as safety when they reflect distrust.
positions.requested_fda_action: Pair override metrics with outcome measures before treating them as evidence of oversight.
positions.public_summary: Supports team-level evaluation but questions whether override rate is a safety measure or a compliance measure.
positions.supporting_text: An override number without an outcome behind it tells a patient nothing.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Results from expert evaluators overstate real-world performance.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require the evaluated user population to match the labeled user population.
positions.public_summary: Supports human-AI evaluation and asks that study designs specify who the human is, since results do not transfer between specialist and generalist users.
positions.supporting_text: A study run with subspecialists tells you nothing about the nurse practitioner who will actually use it.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Vigilance decays with familiarity in ways short studies do not capture.
positions.requested_fda_action: Evaluate oversight behavior over sustained use, not a single session.
positions.public_summary: Supports team-level evaluation from the perspective of a practicing emergency physician and describes reliance creeping in over weeks of use.
positions.supporting_text: In week one I checked everything. By week six I was signing drafts I had skimmed.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Per-site monitoring does not scale across thousands of deployments.
positions.requested_fda_action: Define a sampling-based framework with defined data feeds from sites.
positions.public_summary: Supports a monitoring obligation on manufacturers but wants a scalable framework rather than site-by-site surveillance.
positions.supporting_text: Site-by-site surveillance of every deployment is not a program. It is a headcount problem with no ceiling.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Data extraction and review burden lands on the health system without funding.
positions.requested_fda_action: Specify what sites must provide and what manufacturers must fund or build.
positions.public_summary: Supports monitoring and resists becoming the unpaid operator of manufacturer surveillance obligations.
positions.supporting_text: We are willing to monitor. We are not willing to staff someone else's compliance program.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Without a data pathway, monitoring obligations are unmeetable.
positions.requested_fda_action: Clarify that de-identified performance telemetry is permissible for safety monitoring.
positions.public_summary: Supports manufacturer-led monitoring and offers telemetry as the mechanism, provided privacy constraints are addressed.
positions.supporting_text: The obligation is workable only if the data pathway is explicitly permitted.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Diffuse responsibility means no one holds the signal.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require a named monitoring owner recorded at deployment.
positions.public_summary: Supports shared monitoring with a named accountable party per deployment.
positions.supporting_text: Every deployment should have a name attached to it before go-live.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Sample-based clinician review is unfunded labor.
positions.requested_fda_action: Recognize clinician adjudication as a funded monitoring activity.
positions.public_summary: Supports monitoring and asks that clinician review time be counted as a cost of the program rather than assumed to be free.
positions.supporting_text: Sample-based review by independent clinicians is a good idea with no line item.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Monitoring data may be expected from parties the paper does not name.
positions.requested_fda_action: Clarify whether payer data is in scope for monitoring programs.
positions.public_summary: Raises questions about whether payers would be expected to supply utilization data for monitoring without stating a position on the allocation.
positions.supporting_text: We note that the data most useful for detecting over-utilization sits with payers, who are not mentioned.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Unallocated obligations are unpriceable.
positions.requested_fda_action: Allocate monitoring cost explicitly in any framework.
positions.public_summary: Supports monitoring and asks FDA to say whether the obligation is a cost of the manufacturer or a cost of the deployment.
positions.supporting_text: An obligation no one is assigned is an obligation no one will fund.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Upstream base-model updates fall outside the sponsor's change schedule.
positions.requested_fda_action: Extend change control to cover supplier-initiated changes with a defined re-verification trigger.
positions.public_summary: Supports predetermined change control but says the current PCCP construct does not fit changes the sponsor did not initiate.
positions.supporting_text: We can plan our own releases. The base model changed twice during our submission review.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Deprecation schedules may be shorter than re-verification cycles.
positions.requested_fda_action: Recognize supplier change notice periods in any re-verification requirement.
positions.public_summary: Neutral on the regulatory construct; notes that model deprecation timelines are commercially driven and short.
positions.supporting_text: A ninety-day deprecation notice is standard commercially and may be short for a regulated re-verification.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Sites learn about changed behavior from clinicians, not from release notes.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require advance notice to deployed sites for changes that alter output behavior.
positions.public_summary: Supports change control and asks that sites be notified of behavior-changing updates before they take effect.
positions.supporting_text: The first signal we received was a nurse saying the summaries had started sounding different.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Non-model changes alter behavior as much as model changes.
positions.requested_fda_action: Define prompt, retrieval and tool-access changes as PCCP-eligible modifications.
positions.public_summary: Supports PCCPs for generative products and asks that prompt and retrieval-content changes be treated as modifications with defined verification.
positions.supporting_text: Half of our behavior changes last year were prompt edits. None of them touched the model.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Clearance describes a configuration few sites actually run.
positions.requested_fda_action: Define a minimum local validation step at go-live and after configuration changes.
positions.public_summary: Supports explicit deployment-level assurance expectations and reports material behavior differences between two of its own hospitals.
positions.supporting_text: Same product, same version, two hospitals, materially different output quality.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Sponsors cannot validate every local configuration.
positions.requested_fda_action: Publish supported configuration ranges; treat deviations as site responsibility.
positions.public_summary: Accepts that configuration matters but resists responsibility for site choices made after delivery.
positions.supporting_text: We can define the supported envelope. We cannot test every combination a site will assemble.

positions.stakeholder_concern: There is no infrastructure to observe deployment-level performance.
positions.requested_fda_action: Fund or specify a mechanism for site-level performance reporting.
positions.public_summary: Supports local assurance and warns that no current mechanism captures site-level performance data.
positions.supporting_text: Deployment is where performance is decided and where nobody is currently measuring.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Local validation is only realistic if it is scoped to what a community hospital can execute.
positions.requested_fda_action: Publish a minimum local validation protocol proportionate to site resources.
positions.public_summary: Supports deployment assurance and asks for a template sites can run without a research team.
positions.supporting_text: A validation protocol that needs a biostatistician excludes most of the hospitals in this country.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Errors tied to local formularies are invisible in premarket testing.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require sites to test against their own reference content before go-live.
positions.public_summary: Supports local validation from the perspective of a clinical pharmacist who found formulary-specific errors after go-live.
positions.supporting_text: The model recommended a drug we do not stock, in a dose our protocol does not allow.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Current supplier controls assume component stability.
positions.requested_fda_action: Adapt supplier qualification to cover model versioning and change notification.
positions.public_summary: Supports treating foundation model providers as suppliers under existing quality system expectations.
positions.supporting_text: The supplier control framework already exists. It was written for parts that do not change themselves.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Disclosure obligations may exceed what suppliers can provide.
positions.requested_fda_action: Distinguish behavior-change notification from training data disclosure.
positions.public_summary: Open to change-notification commitments; cautions that full transparency into training data is not commercially feasible.
positions.supporting_text: We can commit to telling customers when behavior changes. We cannot open the training corpus.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Sponsors carry regulatory liability without contractual visibility.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require documented change notification as a condition of reliance.
positions.public_summary: Supports formal supplier obligations and reports difficulty obtaining change notice today.
positions.supporting_text: The liability sits with us and the visibility sits with them.

positions.stakeholder_concern: A master file nobody reads will not be kept current.
positions.requested_fda_action: Specify how a master file would be used in review so suppliers have a reason to maintain it.
positions.public_summary: Supports voluntary master files and says they will only be maintained if FDA staff actually rely on them.
positions.supporting_text: We will keep a master file current if it shortens our customers' reviews. Otherwise it is a document that rots.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Unmanaged supplier risk is unpriceable at the portfolio level.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require sponsors to document supplier change terms in submissions.
positions.public_summary: Supports supplier obligations and notes that model dependency is now a diligence item in every financing.
positions.supporting_text: We now ask every company which model they depend on and what happens when it is deprecated.

positions.stakeholder_concern: An error that executes is different from an error that is displayed.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require a documented intervention point before any clinically consequential action executes.
positions.public_summary: Supports a distinct treatment for action-taking systems and asks for defined intervention points.
positions.supporting_text: A wrong sentence is a draft. A wrong action is an event.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Ambiguous action scope leads to inconsistent site configuration.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require an explicit action inventory in labeling.
positions.public_summary: Supports action-scoped evaluation and proposes describing permitted actions explicitly in labeling.
positions.supporting_text: Say what the system is allowed to do, in a list, in the labeling.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Sites enable capabilities without a formal delegation decision.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require sites to record what authority has been delegated and to whom errors escalate.
positions.public_summary: Supports the direction; notes that delegation decisions are made locally and often informally.
positions.supporting_text: Nobody in our organization signed a document saying the assistant could do that.

positions.stakeholder_concern: A single list of irreversible actions will not fit every clinical setting.
positions.requested_fda_action: Let sponsors define irreversible actions in labeling and test checkpoints against that list.
positions.public_summary: Supports agentic competency testing and asks that irreversible actions be defined by the sponsor rather than by FDA.
positions.supporting_text: What is irreversible in an operating room is not what is irreversible in a scheduling queue.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Patients cannot contest an action they do not know was automated.
positions.requested_fda_action: Require disclosure to patients when an agentic system initiated a care action.
positions.public_summary: Supports human checkpoints and asks that patients be told when an agent, rather than a clinician, initiated an action affecting their care.
positions.supporting_text: Our families want to know whether a person or a program sent the refill.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Tool errors compound across steps in ways single-output testing does not capture.
positions.requested_fda_action: Defer clearance of fully autonomous action until multi-step failure evaluation methods exist.
positions.public_summary: Opposes allowing autonomous action in regulated devices until tool-use failure modes are better characterized.
positions.supporting_text: A chain of five ninety-five-percent steps is a seventy-seven-percent system.

positions.stakeholder_concern: Raises open questions rather than a position.
positions.requested_fda_action: No specific request is made.
positions.public_summary: Discusses intended use boundaries for conversational systems at length without stating a clear recommendation FDA could act on.
